original_value: This paper presents the use of eye tracking data in Magnetic AngularRate Gravity (MARG)-sensor based head orientation estimation. The approach presented here can be deployed in any motion measurement that includes MARG and eye tracking sensors (e.g., rehabilitation robotics or medical diagnostics). The challenge in these mostly indoor applications is the presence of magnetic field disturbances at the location of the MARG-sensor. In this work, eye tracking data (visual fixations) are used to enable zero orientation change updates in the MARG-sensor data fusion chain. The approach is based on a MARG-sensor data fusion filter, an online visual fixation detection algorithm as well as a dynamic angular rate threshold estimation for low latency and adaptive head motion noise parameterization. In this work we use an adaptation of Madgwicks gradient descent filter for MARG-sensor data fusion, but the approach could be used with any other data fusion process. The presented approach does not rely on additional stationary or local environmental references and is therefore self-contained. The proposed system is benchmarked against a Qualisys motion capture system, a gold standard in human motion analysis, showing improved heading accuracy for the MARG-sensor data fusion up to a factor of 0.5 while magnetic disturbance is present.

result.paraphrase: This paper examines how eye-tracking data can be used for head-orientation estimation with Magnetic Angular Rate Gravity (MARG) sensors. The method can be applied to any motion measurement setup that uses MARG and eye-tracking sensors, such as rehabilitation robotics or medical diagnostics. In these mainly indoor settings, a key difficulty is magnetic field interference at the MARG sensor location. Here, visual fixations from eye tracking are used to trigger zero-orientation-change updates within the MARG data-fusion chain. The approach combines a MARG data-fusion filter, an online visual fixation detection algorithm, and dynamic angular-rate threshold estimation for low-latency, adaptive parameterization of head-motion noise. Although this work uses an adaptation of Madgwick’s gradient descent filter for MARG data fusion, the method is compatible with other fusion processes as well. Because it does not depend on additional stationary or local environmental references, the system is self-contained. It is evaluated against a Qualisys motion-capture system, the gold standard in human motion analysis, and shows improved heading accuracy for MARG data fusion by up to a factor of 0.5 when magnetic disturbance is present.
